PT_PROF=3 (skip shadow walk AND skip mesh closest-hit) measured render_ms_best=0.623 ms, render_ms_avg=1.073 ms, gpu_ms_best=0.458 ms — with spp=64, 512x512, samples=16777216, threads_used=8, best of 8 frames.

How I know: it was the last line of the round-5 profiling sweep in the scratch build _prof/ (message #58, which ran `for P in 0 1 2 4 8 3` against the default scene at 64 spp, seed 1). The full sweep in that same output was PT_PROF=0 → gpu 45.352, 1 (no shadow) → 44.051, 2 (no mesh) → 4.773, 4 (no NEE) → 43.171, 8 (glass always-reflect) → 35.764, 3 → 0.458.

What it means: with both mesh-intersection paths disabled the frame collapses to ~0.46 ms of everything else (RNG, camera, NEE arithmetic, floor shading, tone map, accumulation), i.e. ~1% of the frame — confirming the BVH closest-hit walk is the only thing worth optimizing. The contrast between PT_PROF=2 (4.77 ms) and PT_PROF=3 (0.458 ms) also shows that most of that residual 4.77 ms was still shadow-ray *traversal* work (the no-mesh build still walks the tree for shadow rays and only skips the triangle test), which is why the ~1.3 ms attributed to "no shadow" in the full build understates shadow rays' true cost.

How I know: that is the literal stdout of the E0 profiling run in the scratch directory _r8p (the round-7 copy with the split-command-buffer hook), invoked as `PT_SPLIT=1 ./pathtracer --mesh .../stanford-bunny.obj --scene-config ../scene-default.json --benchmark 3 --threads 8 --spp 64 --seed 1` with no diagnostic defines (no PT_DIAG_DEPTH, no PT_DIAG_NOSHADOW). The same run's stderr printed the three per-frame trace-dispatch timings [split] trace_gpu_ms = 30.808 / 30.306 / 30.298, which is why the reported gpu_ms_best of 0.420 is only the combine dispatch: with PT_SPLIT the two dispatches go into separate command buffers and the reported GPU figure comes from the last one. So wall 31.214 ms ≈ trace 30.30 ms + combine 0.42 ms + ~0.5 ms host, i.e. the split build's wall time matched the frozen round-7 binary's ~31 ms at 64 spp and the trace kernel accounted for 98.6% of GPU time — the measurement that sent all round-8 effort into the trace kernel.
